An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. - Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

content.text: I found no spec violations in `/root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/public/index.html` or `/root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/public/app.js`. Both pass, with four small cleanups listed below. I checked the code against the Page section (spec lines 46-63) and searched both files for `http://`/`https://`, `import`/`export`, `console` and `on...=` attributes; none appear. **What I checked against the spec:** - **HTML:** - `` and the only `<h1>` both say "Room bookings". - The form has `novalidate`, and all five fields, ids, types and names are right. Each label sits next to its field rather than wrapping it, with the exact texts. - `#filter-date` has its "Show date" label, and `#show-all` is `type="button"`. `#booking-list` is there, and `#error` has `role="alert"` and starts empty. - There is no `<option>` and no room name. `<script src="/app.js">` has no extra attributes and is the last element in `<body>`. The only inline code is a `<style>` block, which the spec allows. - **Browser APIs:** `app.js` uses only the allowed ones. It is a classic script (an immediately-run function, no import or export) and sets up at once. - **Error messages (`errorMessage`, line 45):** it uses `body.error` only when the body is a non-array object and `error` is a string; otherwise "Request failed.". 204 bodies are never read. - **Unreadable bodies (`request`, line 34):** a non-204 reply whose `json()` fails counts as no reply. - **Last list fetch wins:** `listSequence`/`mine` (lines 90-95) drops every earlier outcome before it can touch the list or `#error`. A successful fetch leaves `#error` alone. The URL adds `?date=<value>` unencoded, as required. - **Booking:** - The handler calls `preventDefault` first, and a submit while Book is disabled sends nothing. - It sends exactly the header `Content-Type: application/json`, with the five raw values and an untrimmed title. - Line 144 re-enables Book right after the reply body has arrived or the request failed, before anything else. On 201 it clears the title and `#error`, then fetches the list again. - **Cancel:** the button is disabled during the request and enabled again when it settles. On no reply it shows "Could not reach the server." and does not fetch the list again. Otherwise it clears `#error` (on 204) or shows the message, then fetches the list again. - **Filter:** only `change` triggers a fetch. Show all clears the value and fetches once, without dispatching any event. - **Plain text:** list items are a text node plus a button, so a title like `<b>x</b>` shows as text, not HTML. **Minor issues:** - **Repeated check:** the long "reached and status 200 and object and array" check appears twice, in `loadList` (lines 96-97) and `loadRooms` (lines 115-116). - **Unused field:** the `failure` value returned at lines 29 and 37 is never read. - **Room filling:** `fillRooms` appends options one at a time in a `forEach`. `renderList` builds the whole list with `replaceChildren` in one call, so the two are inconsistent. - **Unhandled rejection:** if a 200 list reply holds a non-object entry, `renderList` throws, and the call sites (`loadList()` lines 148, 163, 168, 176 and the `change` listener) don't catch it. The page shows no error and the list stays as it was. The server never sends such data, so this is an edge case. ## GRADE Overall: 9/10 Verdict: pass structure: 9 — small single-purpose functions, shallow nesting; room filling appends one by one instead of one replaceChildren call naming: 9 — clear names (request, showOutcomeError, listUrl, bookingItem); `FALLBACK` could say what it falls back for duplication: 8 — the reply-shape check is repeated in loadList and loadRooms size: 10 — 177-line script, every function well under 50 lines errors: 9 — every spec failure path is handled with friendly messages; a malformed booking entry would cause an unhandled rejection tests: n/a — the testing section writes the tests security: 10 — everything shown via textContent/text nodes, no secrets, no inline handlers leftovers: 9 — no console or debug code; unused `failure` field in request() Fixes: - /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/public/app.js:96 move the "reached && status && isPlainObject(body) && Array.isArray(body[key])" check into one helper (e.g. `listFrom(outcome, status, key)`) and use it at lines 96 and 115 - /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/public/app.js:29 drop the unused `failure` field (also line 37), returning `{ reached: false }` - /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/public/app.js:104 build the options with `rooms.map(...)` and set them with one `roomSelect.replaceChildren(...options)`, the same way as renderList - /root/bench-runs/h4-fad7c86d/public/app.js:79 add a catch where loadList runs (or check each entry is an object) so a malformed list entry shows "Request failed." instead of an unhandled rejection
